question: How does chronic psychological stress typically affect food cravings?

options.A: It increases a natural desire for raw vegetables and water
options.B: It raises cortisol and triggers cravings for fatty, sugary foods
options.C: It forces the digestive system to absorb fewer total calories
options.D: It completely stops the body from digesting any proteins

explanation: You got it! High cortisol from stress tricks the brain into seeking out dense, comforting, high-calorie foods for quick energy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: Why should a nurse remind patients using mydriatic (pupil-dilating) drops to wear sunglasses outside?

options.A: The medication changes the natural color of the iris
options.B: Bright sunlight can make the cornea swell up rapidly
options.C: Ultraviolet rays will destroy the active drug
options.D: Their widened pupils let in way too much glaring light

explanation: When pupils are forced wide open by drops, they can't shrink down to block bright sunlight. Sunglasses save the patient from painful glare! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why is it so important to keep the initial scope of a test of change very small?

options.A: It prevents overwhelming staff and keeps potential disruption to a minimum
options.B: It guarantees that no data will ever be lost during the shift
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever expand the project later on
options.D: It satisfies legal requirements for experimental medical research

explanation: Keeping things tiny means your team won't get stressed out, and if the idea flops, nobody gets hurt and patient care stays safe. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which type of family planning method is generally considered safest for a breastfeeding mother in the early weeks?

options.A: Progestin-only methods
options.B: Emergency morning-after pills
options.C: High-dose estrogen patches
options.D: Combined oral contraceptives

explanation: Progestin-only options (like mini-pills or certain injectables) won't mess with her breastmilk supply, making them a great choice for nursing mums. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: What nursing action should be performed immediately after removing the flatus tube?

options.A: Check the patient's blood pressure
options.B: Insert a new tube into the urethra
options.C: Clean and dry the perianal area
options.D: Administer a strong oral laxative

explanation: Cleaning the perianal area removes any residual lubricant or discharge, ensuring skin integrity and patient comfort. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What happens during the implementation stage of a health plan?

options.A: The health committee writes down initial budget guesses
options.B: All nurses retire and hand over duties to administrators
options.C: The community is surveyed to see if they want a clinic
options.D: The planned health programs and services are put into action

explanation: Implementation is the active phase where your written plans finally turn into real care for people. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h6)

question: What type of energy does an MRI machine use to take pictures of inside the body?

options.A: High-dose ionizing X-ray radiation
options.B: Powerful magnetic fields and radio waves
options.C: Injected radioactive liquid tracers
options.D: High-frequency sound waves

explanation: No radiation here! MRIs use massive magnets and radio waves to create super detailed pictures of your soft tissues and joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main reason nurses use functional assessment tools in a rehab ward?

options.A: To calculate the exact date of hospital discharge
options.B: To measure how much assistance a patient needs with daily activities
options.C: To determine daily caloric requirements
options.D: To diagnose underlying genetic mutations

explanation: You got it! These tools help us clearly see how independent a patient is and track their progress over time. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why are functional emergency referral systems so important for pregnant women in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policy requires all babies to be born in teaching hospitals
options.B: Patients prefer to pay higher fees at tertiary hospitals rather than local clinics
options.C: Primary health clinics cannot manage severe obstetric emergencies like ruptured uterus or eclampsia
options.D: Primary health centers do not keep any medical records of pregnant women

explanation: Local clinics are great for routine antenatal care, but if a life-threatening emergency like severe eclampsia happens, patients need quick transport to a bigger hospital with a doctor and blood bank. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h7)

question: What is the very first stop in the brainstem where all taste nerve fibers meet?

options.A: Thalamus
options.B: Nucleus of the solitary tract
options.C: Hypothalamus
options.D: Gustatory cortex

explanation: Taste signals traveling through cranial nerves VII, IX, and X all make their first brainstem stop at the nucleus of the solitary tract in the medulla. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T10#GNS211_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why is giving plain water unnecessary for a fully breastfed infant living in a very hot climate?

options.A: Infants cannot swallow water safely during their first few months
options.B: Breast milk is made mostly of water and satisfies the infant's thirst
options.C: Hot weather stops the infant from feeling thirsty
options.D: Water causes immediate stomach pain in newborn babies

explanation: Breast milk contains about eighty-eight percent water, which is more than enough to keep a baby hydrated even in hot weather. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h1)

question: Why is Post-Abortion Care (PAC) considered a complete, all-round care model?

options.A: It involves police reports for every single case
options.B: It delays discharge until lab results are ready
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, family planning, and emotional support
options.D: It focuses only on theatre surgeries

explanation: PAC looks at the whole patient—healing her body, supporting her emotions, and helping her plan for the future. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h6)

question: What procedure is often needed if leftover placental tissue is causing ongoing postpartum sepsis?

options.A: Total abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: Appendectomy
options.C: Evacuation of the uterus
options.D: Bilateral tubal ligation

explanation: If dead placental tissue is trapped inside, antibiotics alone won't clear it. We need to gently clear out the uterus to help the mother heal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h6)

question: What is a major error a nurse can make during community mobilisation?

options.A: Asking local leaders for permission to enter the village
options.B: Taking over leadership and making decisions for the community
options.C: Teaching mothers how to prepare oral rehydration salt
options.D: Working with local volunteers to clean up the environment

explanation: Nurses should facilitate and empower, not take control and rob the community of their self-reliance. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: Why are secondary complications so dangerous for patients with brain or nerve injuries?

options.A: They can worsen the initial injury and cause further damage
options.B: They disappear without any medical intervention
options.C: They always reverse the effects of the primary disease
options.D: They only affect the peripheral nervous system

explanation: Secondary problems put extra stress on a body that is already struggling, often leading to a much worse outcome than the original injury. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h1)

question: Why does the body slow down its metabolism during long periods of starvation?

options.A: To conserve remaining energy stores and prolong survival
options.B: To build up extra muscle tissue in the limbs
options.C: To prepare the digestive tract for a heavy meal
options.D: To increase physical activity levels automatically

explanation: It is a brilliant survival mechanism. When food is scarce, the body dials down its energy use so it doesn't burn through its fat and muscle too fast. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h6)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding equipment preparation for ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: Checking battery power and light brightness on the ophthalmoscope
options.B: Calibrating the internal magnifying glass to match the patient's age
options.C: Sterilizing the handle and head of the device in an autoclave machine
options.D: Replacing the handheld lens with a digital camera attachment

explanation: The nurse must verify that the handheld scope has working batteries and sufficient illumination before the clinician begins the exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is a major non-medical challenge that delays emergency survival in many developing areas?

options.A: Strict government regulations on the use of intravenous fluids
options.B: A lack of interest in modern medicine among rural community members
options.C: Delays in reaching a health facility due to financial and transport challenges
options.D: Excessive availability of free ambulance services on major roads

explanation: Transportation bottlenecks and money hurdles often delay patients from getting to the hospital on time. Every minute counts in an emergency! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful medical or surgical option for managing tubal factor infertility?

options.A: Prolonged bed rest and pelvic massage
options.B: In Vitro Fertilization
options.C: Diagnostic and operative laparoscopy
options.D: Intrauterine insemination

explanation: Bed rest and massages cannot fix structural problems or short lengths in the fallopian tubes. Medical treatments like IVF or surgery are needed for that. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h7)

question: Why are older adults at a much higher risk for dehydration?

options.A: Their bodies require zero water intake after age sixty
options.B: They sweat significantly more than younger adults
options.C: Fluid absorption is blocked completely in the stomach
options.D: They have a blunted thirst response and may not feel thirsty

explanation: The natural body mechanism that tells us we are thirsty slows down with age, so older adults often won't drink unless we gently remind and encourage them. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h6)

question: Why is an MRI scan so helpful when evaluating a patient with suspected CJD?

options.A: It checks the electrical activity of skeletal muscles.
options.B: It reveals characteristic patterns of brain tissue damage.
options.C: It measures the exact level of circulating antibodies.
options.D: It clears away abnormal prion protein deposits safely.

explanation: Spot on! An MRI can show distinct bright spots and damage patterns in specific areas of the brain, guiding the medical team. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why is your Eustachian tube so important?

options.A: Translating vibrations into nerve signals
options.B: Secreting protective earwax
options.C: Equalizing air pressure in the middle ear
options.D: Amplifying high-pitched sounds

explanation: Ever felt your ears 'pop' when swallowing or yawning? That is your Eustachian tube balancing out air pressure so your eardrum stays comfortable. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h3)

question: A teenager finds it hard to say no to friends pushing them into early sex. How can a nurse best help?

options.A: Help the teenager identify personal values and practice clear boundary-setting skills
options.B: Provide the teenager with a prescription for oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Tell the teenager that peer pressure is completely harmless and easy to ignore
options.D: Instruct the teenager to cut off all contact with every friend immediately

explanation: Wonderful nursing approach! Teaching teens how to set boundaries and speak up with confidence helps them stand strong against peer pressure. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h4)

question: Why is it important to reverse (back) a wheelchair when going down a steep ramp?

options.A: To make it much easier for the nurse to steer the front wheels
options.B: To prevent the patient from pitching forward out of the chair
options.C: To keep the patient's feet from touching the ground below
options.D: To protect the rubber tires from wearing down too quickly

explanation: Going down forward on a steep incline shifts the center of gravity and can cause the patient to tumble out of the seat. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h5)

question: What is the main goal of giving recommendations for future research?

options.A: To give graduate students easy thesis topics they do not have to think about
options.B: To guide subsequent studies based on current gaps and unanswered questions
options.C: To prove that the current study answered every single question in nursing
options.D: To ensure the original researcher gets paid for all future grants

explanation: You've got this! No single study answers everything. Pointing out what's left to discover helps the next wave of researchers. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T5#GNS224_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why is the skin considered our body's primary shield?

options.A: It sits right between our internal organs and the outside world.
options.B: It produces all our red blood cells.
options.C: It pumps nutrients directly into underlying muscles.
options.D: It filters waste straight out of our bloodstream.

explanation: Spot on! Because skin covers our entire outside, it acts as our very first line of defense against everyday hazards. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h1)

question: A lab report shows normal skin bacteria growing in a urine sample that was collected carelessly. What is this called?

options.A: Contamination
options.B: Immunization
options.C: Pathogenicity
options.D: Sterilization

explanation: Oops! When harmless germs from the skin accidentally hitch a ride into our sample collection, we call it specimen contamination. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the proper nursing action when a competent patient insists on leaving the hospital before treatment is complete?

options.A: Explain the risks and have them sign a discharge against medical advice form
options.B: Ignore the request and refuse to give them their personal clothes
options.C: Call the police immediately to physically lock the patient inside the room
options.D: Hide the patient's shoes so they cannot walk out of the ward

explanation: A competent adult has the right to leave, but the nurse must warn them of potential dangers and document the event by having them sign a DAMA form. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why does taking strong, broad-spectrum antibiotics often lead to an annoying yeast infection?

options.A: It kills protective lactobacilli bacteria
options.B: It increases the production of vaginal glycogen
options.C: It lowers overall body temperature
options.D: It directly stimulates fungal spore production

explanation: Antibiotics are great, but they aren't picky—they wipe out our protective friendly bacteria right along with the bad ones, leaving yeast free to party! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the main goal of monitoring a patient after giving them a medication?

options.A: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay
options.B: To evaluate therapeutic effectiveness and watch for adverse reactions
options.C: To write a long essay about the patient's medical history
options.D: To prove to hospital management that nurses are working hard

explanation: Checking on your patient later lets you see if the drug is actually working and helps you catch any side effects early. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why is a study that just repeats common knowledge without any new angle considered weak?

options.A: It will automatically cause patients to experience adverse events
options.B: It requires too much expensive laboratory equipment
options.C: It is illegal under international medical guidelines
options.D: It fails to advance the existing body of professional knowledge

explanation: Correct! As nursing students, we want our studies to push the profession forward, not just restate things everyone already knows. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is considered the gold standard method for measuring energy expenditure in a clinical setting?

options.A: Indirect calorimetry
options.B: Standard height-weight charts
options.C: Bioelectrical impedance
options.D: Skinfold caliper testing

explanation: Indirect calorimetry is a neat clinical test that calculates metabolic rate by analyzing the oxygen a patient inhales and the carbon dioxide they exhale. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is a key feature that makes a tertiary health facility unique?

options.A: It only handles uncomplicated outpatient malaria cases
options.B: It is the first point of contact in a rural village
options.C: It provides basic immunization only
options.D: It serves as a center for training and medical research

explanation: Tertiary hospitals (like our teaching hospitals) do double duty: they provide advanced patient care while training future healthcare heroes and conducting medical research. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is an ovarian cyst?

options.A: A solid tumor growing inside the uterus
options.B: A complete blockage of the vaginal canal
options.C: An infection of the fallopian tubes
options.D: A fluid-filled sac on or inside an ovary

explanation: Ovarian cysts are pockets or sacs filled with fluid that develop on or inside the ovarian tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h1)

question: Why is building a trusting relationship between the nurse and the pregnant woman so important?

options.A: It encourages the woman to report health problems and return for follow-up visits
options.B: It prevents the husband from being involved in family health decisions
options.C: It eliminates the need for any laboratory tests during pregnancy
options.D: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any complications

explanation: Trust reduces anxiety and ensures women feel safe sharing their symptoms and returning to the facility for care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)?

options.A: To measure the absolute least amount of protein a sick patient requires
options.B: To identify the highest daily nutrient intake unlikely to cause harm
options.C: To determine the standard portion size for hospital meal trays
options.D: To calculate the minimum amount of calories needed to survive a fast

explanation: The UL acts as a safety guard, showing the absolute highest amount of a nutrient you can take daily before risking toxicity. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h3)

question: What is the dangerous practice of using the same syringe barrel for more than one patient called?

options.A: Syringe reuse
options.B: Z-track administration
options.C: Aseptic transfer
options.D: Vial reconstitution

explanation: You nailed it! Reusing syringes—even if you change the needle—transfers microscopic amounts of blood and fluids between patients, spreading serious infections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: A clinic manager wants to hike drug prices to build a staff canteen. Why does this break DRF rules?

options.A: Staff canteens are illegal in public hospitals
options.B: Drug prices are fixed permanently by international law
options.C: DRF funds must be reinvested strictly into drug procurement and facility operations linked to the fund
options.D: Only the federal government can adjust drug prices

explanation: Think of DRF money as sacred! It's ring-fenced strictly for buying more lifesaving medicines, not for building canteens or other unrelated projects. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T5#GNS215_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why might doctors order a thyroid test for a patient with severe hyperemesis?

options.A: It helps check the exact gestational age of the fetus
options.B: Thyroid failure is the primary cause of all pregnancy vomiting
options.C: High levels of hCG can temporarily stimulate the thyroid gland
options.D: Thyroid medication is always used to cure morning sickness

explanation: Because hCG hormone looks a bit like thyroid-stimulating hormone, sky-high pregnancy hormones can trick the thyroid into working overtime. Brilliant clinical insight! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h5)

question: Why are teenagers often more prone to screen addiction than older adults?

options.A: Their prefrontal cortex is still maturing, making impulse control difficult
options.B: They have more financial resources to purchase high-end gadgets
options.C: They spend less time sleeping than adults do on average
options.D: Their eyes are more sensitive to the blue light emitted by screens

explanation: Think about brain development! The part of the brain that helps with self-control and good judgment is still growing in teens, making it harder to put the phone down. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for teaching a patient with an endocrine condition?

options.A: Providing clear written action plans for emergency symptoms
options.B: Tailoring the teaching session to the patient's cultural background
options.C: Giving long medical lectures without checking for understanding
options.D: Using a return-demonstration approach for practical skills

explanation: Correct! Long, boring lectures don't help anyone learn. We always want interactive teaching and plenty of feedback! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h5)

question: Why is teaching a mother the correct way for her baby to latch crucial during breastfeeding?

options.A: It guarantees the infant will sleep through the night
options.B: It stops the baby from spitting up any milk
options.C: It prevents maternal nipple pain and ensures effective milk transfer
options.D: It forces the mother's milk to change from colostrum instantly

explanation: A good latch is a win-win: it keeps the mother's nipples safe from painful cracks and helps the baby get a full tummy efficiently! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: What should a patient with a respiratory infection wear when moving outside their isolation room?

options.A: Cover the patient completely with a sterile plastic sheet
options.B: Transport the patient only during night shift hours
options.C: Ensure the patient walks without any staff assistance
options.D: Have the patient wear a surgical mask during transport

explanation: Exactly! Having the patient wear a mask traps any stray respiratory droplets right at the source while you walk them through the hospital corridors. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h7)

question: During a special ultrasound procedure (saline infusion sonohysterography), sterile saline is gently injected into the uterus. Why?

options.A: To distend the cavity and create a sharp contrast for the ultrasound images
options.B: To numb the internal walls of the uterus prior to a biopsy
options.C: To completely dissolve small endometrial polyps without medication
options.D: To wash away any bacterial infections before surgery starts

explanation: You got it! The fluid puffs up the uterine space like blowing up a tiny balloon, making it much easier for the ultrasound to spot polyps or fibroids. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h4)

question: Which chemical compound is commonly used for disinfecting blood spills on hard surfaces due to its quick action and low cost?

options.A: Liquid paraffin oil
options.B: Normal saline solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide cream
options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

explanation: Sodium hypochlorite, commonly known as bleach, is an affordable and effective disinfectant for clearing up blood spills. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is one of the very early physical signs of pregnancy you might spot on a woman's breasts due to extra blood flow?

options.A: Shrinkage of the overall breast size
options.B: Complete absence of areolar pigmentation
options.C: Prominent and visible superficial veins
options.D: Active secretion of mature white milk

explanation: Because the body sends extra blood to the breasts to prepare for feeding, the veins near the surface become much easier to see. Neat physiological adaptation, right? [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h3)

question: Which of these is considered a geological natural disaster?

options.A: Flood
options.B: Earthquake
options.C: Heatwave
options.D: Hurricane

explanation: Geological disasters start from forces deep beneath the earth, like earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, while floods and hurricanes are weather-driven. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h2)

question: What does an anterior body landmark refer to?

options.A: A structure located on the front of the body
options.B: A structure located on the back of the body
options.C: A bony prominence found only on the skull
options.D: A deep internal organ with no surface visibility

explanation: Anterior landmarks are situated on the front or ventral surface of the human body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why must sexual partners be treated at the same time when someone has a bacterial STI?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory insurance claim covers the cost of the initial diagnostic workup
options.B: To speed up the metabolic clearance of the antibiotic through the kidneys
options.C: To prevent the patient from becoming immediately reinfected after finishing treatment
options.D: To prevent the development of drug-resistant fungal strains in the community

explanation: Treating partners simultaneously stops the back-and-forth 'ping-pong' spread of the infection between couples. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is the main way ordinary Nigerians pay for their healthcare needs?

options.A: Community health funds
options.B: Federal health insurance
options.C: Out-of-pocket payments
options.D: Employer-paid retainerships

explanation: You got it! Most Nigerians pay cash straight from their pockets for every consultation, lab test, and prescription whenever they visit a clinic. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h3)

question: What does a decline in 'executive function' look like for a patient?

options.A: Trouble with planning, organizing, and solving problems
options.B: Constant involuntary shaking of the hands
options.C: A complete inability to feel physical pain
options.D: Sudden loss of the ability to swallow food

explanation: Executive functions are like the brain's manager—they help us plan our day, organize tasks, and solve everyday problems. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h4)

question: How many main tiers make up Nigeria's public healthcare system?

options.A: Three distinct levels of care
options.B: Five distinct levels of care
options.C: Two distinct levels of care
options.D: Four distinct levels of care

explanation: Think of Nigeria's health setup like a ladder with three steps: primary, secondary, and tertiary. Each level is built to handle specific types of health needs in our communities! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h1)

question: A home nurse finds a family completely exhausted from caring for an aging relative with dementia. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the family to social authorities for failing to provide basic care
options.B: Tell the family they must immediately place the relative in a permanent hospital
options.C: Advise them to stop providing care and leave the patient alone during the day
options.D: Connect the family with community support services and respite care options

explanation: Caregiver burnout is so real! Linking exhausted families with professional relief and respite care helps everyone keep going safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is a virtual health community?

options.A: An online space where people connect for health support
options.B: A physical clinic equipped with virtual reality headsets
options.C: A government database of all registered nurses in a country
options.D: An emergency ambulance fitted with satellite navigation

explanation: You got it! Think of online support groups, health forums, and social media pages where people share health tips. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why do nurses avoid using chemical names of drugs during routine clinical practice?

options.A: Chemical names change every time a new company manufactures the drug
options.B: Chemical names are strictly reserved for pharmacy dispensing staff only
options.C: Chemical names are too complex and difficult to use safely in daily care
options.D: Chemical names only describe the inactive filler ingredients in the tablet

explanation: Chemical names are full of complex molecular descriptions. Imagine trying to read one out quickly during an emergency ward round—way too tricky! That's why we stick to generic and brand names. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h1)

question: What does a 'feasible' research project mean for a student?

options.A: Whether the hospital will change its name after the study
options.B: Whether the research topic is popular on social media
options.C: How many international awards the study might win
options.D: Whether the study can actually be done with available resources

explanation: Feasibility is just about being realistic—making sure you have enough time, money, and materials to finish the study without burning out. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h3)

question: A patient handles ward stress by going for brisk walks and talking things through with a close friend. How would a nurse label this response?

options.A: Psychotic
options.B: Adaptive
options.C: Regressive
options.D: Maladaptive

explanation: Spot on! Exercising and leaning on a support system are classic healthy, adaptive ways to handle pressure. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which organ system uses hormones to regulate slow, long-term body processes?

options.A: The nervous system
options.B: The muscular system
options.C: The endocrine system
options.D: The respiratory system

explanation: Glands in the endocrine system secrete chemical messengers called hormones directly into the bloodstream to control distant target organs over time. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h3)

question: What major hazard happens when sharps disposal boxes are allowed to become overfilled?

options.A: Rapid evaporation of liquid medications stored inside
options.B: Chemical reactions that dissolve the plastic bin
options.C: Foul odors spreading throughout the hospital ward
options.D: Higher risk of accidental needle pricks for staff and waste handlers

explanation: Exactly! When bins are stuffed too full, needles start poking out and endangering everyone nearby. Always swap out sharps bins before they hit the fill line! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h8)

question: What makes Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) different from traditional surveys?

options.A: It focuses only on collecting numerical laboratory test results
options.B: It is conducted entirely by foreign experts without local input
options.C: It requires expensive computers and satellite internet connections
options.D: It actively involves community members in analyzing their own conditions

explanation: Well done! PRA puts the community in the driver's seat to evaluate their own challenges. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic, telltale sign of digoxin toxicity?

options.A: Sudden uncontrollable muscle twitching in legs
options.B: Turning of the skin to a bright red color
options.C: Seeing yellow-green halos around lights
options.D: Complete loss of the sense of hearing

explanation: Classic nursing board exam favorite! Seeing yellow-green halos or fuzzy lights is a huge red flag that there is too much digoxin in the patient's system. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h7)

question: What must a nurse have before filing a report for suspected child abuse?

options.A: Absolute physical proof and a signed confession from the parent
options.B: Written permission from the hospital legal department
options.C: Reasonable cause to suspect maltreatment based on observations
options.D: Confirmation from at least two senior medical doctors

explanation: You don't need 100% hard proof to report. A reasonable, professional suspicion based on what you see is enough to take action. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h6)

question: If a patient has severe liver disease and cannot make enough plasma proteins, what sign are they most likely to show?

options.A: Excessive dark stools
options.B: Generalized tissue swelling
options.C: Rapid hair loss
options.D: Sudden high fever

explanation: Spot on! Without enough albumin to hold fluid in the vessels, water leaks out into the body tissues, causing swelling (edema) that you will often see in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why do nurses give medications through an IV line instead of having the patient swallow a pill?

options.A: It lasts much longer in the bloodstream than oral pills.
options.B: It prevents all known systemic side effects from occurring.
options.C: It is completely painless for every patient receiving treatment.
options.D: It provides a much faster onset of drug action in the body.

explanation: Spot on! Because IV fluids go straight into the bloodstream, the body skips the digestive tract entirely and goes to work right away. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T6#GNS311_U4_T6_h1)

question: What do we call the mature, fluid-filled follicle that is fully ready to release an egg?

options.A: Corpus albicans
options.B: Primordial follicle
options.C: Graafian follicle
options.D: Atretic follicle

explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, mature stage before it bursts open to release the egg. Great landmark to remember in reproductive anatomy! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which requirement must be met before skilled home health nursing care can officially start?

options.A: The family must purchase a private hospital bed
options.B: The patient must win a local community award
options.C: A licensed physician must order the care
options.D: The nurse must live with the patient full-time

explanation: Home health services require a formal medical order from a doctor just like any other prescription or therapy. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h8)

question: When is the best time to perform airway suctioning on a ventilated patient?

options.A: When clinical indicators like secretions or coughing are present
options.B: Every single hour on the exact hour without fail
options.C: Only when the high-pressure alarm rings twice
options.D: Immediately before every meal or tube-feeding cycle

explanation: We don't suction on a rigid schedule because it can irritate the airway and lower oxygen levels. Instead, we listen, assess, and suction only when the patient actually needs it. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of barrier nursing?

options.A: To completely cure chronic infectious diseases
options.B: To stop pathogens from spreading between people
options.C: To speed up the healing of surgical wounds
options.D: To replace the need for routine handwashing

explanation: Barrier nursing uses physical blocks to prevent germs from moving from one person or surface to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is an example of a 'forcing function' used to keep patients safe in a hospital?

options.A: Verbally reminding nurses to check blood pressure twice a shift
options.B: Hanging warning signs near every medication storage cabinet
options.C: Punishing staff members who forget to sign documentation sheets
options.D: Feeding tubes that physically cannot connect to intravenous lines

explanation: A forcing function is brilliant because it uses physical design to make a dangerous mistake literally impossible—like making ports that only fit the correct tubing! [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why do we count water as a nutrient even though it gives us zero calories?

options.A: It breaks down into simple sugars inside the stomach lining
options.B: It is essential for life, acting as a medium for all metabolic reactions
options.C: It stimulates the production of digestive enzymes in the pancreas
options.D: It converts directly into structural tissue during growth phases

explanation: Correct! A nutrient is anything needed for survival and body chemistry—it doesn't have to provide energy to be vital. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h4)

question: What do the four letters in the PDSA quality improvement cycle stand for?

options.A: Plan, Do, Study, Act
options.B: Prepare, Design, Streamline, Assess
options.C: Predict, Document, Sort, Analyze
options.D: Practice, Direct, Secure, Apply

explanation: PDSA is a handy little cycle we use to test changes: Plan your test, Do it, Study the results, and Act on what you learned! [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the best feeding practice recommended for an infant's first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding
options.B: Water and thin maize pap
options.C: Mashed family meals
options.D: Goat milk and infant formula

explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, nutrients, and antibodies a baby needs for the first six months. Nothing else is required! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)

question: Some food handlers are struggling with hygiene rules because they find English difficult. What should the nurse supervisor do?

options.A: Stop doing hygiene training and rely only on surprise inspections
options.B: Punish the workers for failing to read the English instruction manual
options.C: Conduct training sessions using the local language and visual demonstrations
options.D: Report the workers to the police for breaking environmental laws

explanation: Adapting how you teach to match your audience ensures everyone understands these life-saving safety practices. Great clinical judgment! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h7)

question: Even if a brain tumor is benign (non-cancerous), why can it still turn into a medical emergency?

options.A: The immune system attacks the tumor and causes severe swelling.
options.B: The rigid skull prevents expansion and causes dangerous pressure.
options.C: Benign tumors always turn into fast-growing cancers over time.
options.D: Benign brain tumors immediately destroy all local nerve cells.

explanation: Great thinking! The human skull is like a hard box that cannot stretch. Even a benign growth takes up precious space inside, crowding the brain and causing dangerous pressure. Location matters just as much as cell type! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h1)

question: Which of the following is a primary way the community environment influences health?

options.A: Replacing the need for individual personal hygiene
options.B: Providing access to safe water, markets, and local clinics
options.C: Ensuring every citizen has a high-paying professional job
options.D: Eliminating all infectious diseases from the environment

explanation: Basic community infrastructure like clean water and nearby health clinics directly dictates physical well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the big downside of using a simple flat daily rate (per diem) to cost nursing care?

options.A: it is illegal to use in modern public hospitals
options.B: It ignores individual patient needs and care complexity
options.C: It only calculates the cost of surgical procedures
options.D: It requires complex computer software for every shift

explanation: A flat daily rate assumes every single patient costs the same to nurse, which isn't fair because a critical patient needs way more work than someone resting comfortably. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: What tool do traditional practitioners commonly use for scarification?

options.A: Electric tattoo needles
options.B: Locally forged blades
options.C: Sterile surgical scalpels
options.D: Disposable laser pens

explanation: Traditional practitioners usually rely on locally crafted metal blades or sharp stones rather than sterile hospital equipment. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h2)

question: Why should you avoid heavy medical jargon when breaking the news of a death to family members?

options.A: It forces the family to ask the physician for translation
options.B: It is against hospital accreditation rules to use medical terms
options.C: It can cause confusion and prevent them from grasping the reality of the loss
options.D: It makes the nurse sound unprofessional and uneducated

explanation: Spot on! Using plain, simple language ensures grieving relatives truly understand what happened without getting confused by big words. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h8)

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a nurse on a hospital ward?

options.A: Being immune from any form of peer review or performance evaluation
options.B: Working night shifts without physical security guards on the ward
options.C: Never experiencing stress or fatigue during clinical duties
options.D: Feeling safe to report errors and speak up without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: You got it! Psychological safety means trust—knowing you can speak up honestly to protect your patients. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h6)

question: Which type of precautions calls for wearing a specially fitted N95 respirator mask?

options.A: Droplet Precautions
options.B: Airborne Precautions
options.C: Standard Precautions
options.D: Contact Precautions

explanation: You nailed it! Airborne bugs float around on tiny particles, so we need that high-level N95 protection to keep our lungs safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h3)

question: A stroke patient is struggling with swallowing food safely and speaking clearly. Who should the nurse call for help?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Social worker
options.C: Prosthetist
options.D: Physiotherapist

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at helping patients overcome both communication hurdles and swallowing issues (dysphagia). [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of working with a mobilized community for a nurse?

options.A: Health messages spread easily through local networks
options.B: All diseases are completely eradicated overnight
options.C: Nurses no longer need to write patient records
options.D: The government stops paying salaries to health workers

explanation: When a community is mobilized, people talk to each other about health, making health education spread fast. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why should you as a nurse care about what your patient likes or is used to eating?

options.A: Hospital management requires a daily report on tribal food choices
options.B: It helps the nurse order the exact same meal for every ward bed
options.C: Dietary habits directly impact wound healing and recovery speed
options.D: Patients refuse medications if their food preferences are ignored

explanation: Spot on! When patients enjoy their food and it fits their background, they eat better, heal faster, and avoid poor nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h1)

question: Which patient has the highest risk of developing endometrial cancer?

options.A: A 22-year-old athlete using combination oral contraceptives
options.B: A 65-year-old obese woman with a history of late menopause
options.C: A 30-year-old woman who has given birth to four children
options.D: A 45-year-old woman with regular 28-day menstrual cycles

explanation: Correct! Older age, obesity, and late menopause all mean a longer time of being exposed to estrogen without a break. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T23#GNS216_U5_T23_h3)

question: Why does our sense of taste naturally react strongly against bitter foods?

options.A: To identify energy-rich carbohydrate sources
options.B: To maintain normal blood electrolyte levels
options.C: To signal the presence of dietary protein
options.D: To warn the body against potential poisons

explanation: Think of bitterness as your body's built-in alarm system! It evolved to help us spot dangerous toxins or plant alkaloids before we swallow them. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T10#GNS211_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why should we involve parents and community leaders in adolescent health programs?

options.A: To shift cultural norms and build supportive safety nets for teens
options.B: To give adults total control over adolescent personal decisions
options.C: To ensure healthcare facilities collect more financial profit
options.D: To eliminate the need for professional nursing staff

explanation: Correct! When community leaders and parents are on board, stigma drops and teenagers find a safer network to ask for help. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T8#GNS312_U3_T8_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of inflammation in the human body?

options.A: To decrease blood flow to injured areas
options.B: To permanently increase the body temperature
options.C: To speed up the breakdown of red blood cells
options.D: To destroy foreign invaders and repair damaged tissue

explanation: The immune system initiates inflammation specifically to neutralize threats and heal injuries. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why must nurses monitor vital signs very closely in a patient with a suspected brainstem injury involving the medulla?

options.A: Cardiovascular and respiratory failure can happen suddenly
options.B: Kidney failure develops within the first hour
options.C: Blood pressure medications stop working entirely
options.D: Core body temperature always drops below normal

explanation: Because the medulla houses the primary breathing and heart rate centers, injury here directly threatens life support functions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h6)

question: What do geographical boundaries (like rivers or roads) give to a traditional community?

options.A: Clear physical limits and a defined space for service delivery
options.B: Guaranteed financial funding from international agencies
options.C: Absolute immunity from infectious disease outbreaks
options.D: Complete isolation from neighboring populations

explanation: Physical borders make it easy for nurses to map out an area and plan where to bring healthcare services. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is studying an entire population usually impractical for a nursing study?

options.A: Research ethics committees do not allow large studies
options.B: Patients refuse to answer questions if everyone is included
options.C: Statistical software cannot process large amounts of data
options.D: It is too expensive, time-consuming, and logistically difficult

explanation: Exactly! Imagine trying to interview every single nurse or patient in the whole country—you'd spend all your time and money moving around. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h1)

question: How do nurses usually record how much of a meal a patient actually ate in the chart?

options.A: Counting every individual grain of rice
options.B: Taking a photo of the tray after eating
options.C: Weighing food scraps on a gram scale
options.D: Percentage estimation of the meal eaten

explanation: That's right! We estimate intake in quarters (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) to quickly track how much nourishment they got. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h5)

question: Why is the federal VAPP Act alone sometimes not enough to stop FGM across all Nigerian states?

options.A: States must pass their own version (domesticate the act) before local courts can enforce it
options.B: Traditional rulers have complete immunity from federal laws
options.C: The federal government leaves rural areas out of national laws
options.D: Federal laws expire automatically after five years

explanation: You got it! Nigeria operates under a federal system where state legislatures must domesticate federal laws for them to be fully operational and enforceable locally. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which leadership style is most appropriate during a sudden cardiac arrest emergency?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Laissez-faire
options.C: Delegative
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: An emergency requires fast, clear, direct instructions without debates, making autocratic leadership essential. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h5)

question: Your patient just had talc pleurodesis and is crying out in sharp pain. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient that chest pain is completely abnormal
options.B: Encourage the patient to take shallow, rapid breaths
options.C: Immediately pull out the patient's chest tube
options.D: Administer the prescribed pain medication promptly

explanation: Compassionate care is key! Sclerosants cause heavy inflammation and pain. Giving prescribed pain relief quickly helps your patient relax and take deep breaths again. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T12#GNS125_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you should do if a patient's tracheostomy tube accidentally pops out shortly after surgery?

options.A: Call the surgeon and wait at the bedside
options.B: Cover the open wound with sterile gauze permanently
options.C: Administer oral cough syrup to calm the patient
options.D: Attempt reinsertion using the bedside obturator

explanation: Don't panic! A fresh stoma can close up in minutes, blocking the airway. Grab that bedside obturator and try to pop the tube back in right away. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do we often see higher maternal and child mortality rates in rural Nigerian communities compared to big cities?

options.A: Rural populations have a higher birth rate per family
options.B: Rural residents completely reject modern medicine due to cultural laws
options.C: Urban populations have stronger immune systems from birth
options.D: Rural areas have limited access to equipped health facilities and skilled birth attendants

explanation: Spot on! Bad roads, long distances, and lack of well-equipped clinics mean emergencies take too long to reach help. This is why community health nursing is so vital in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h2)

question: Why do emergency planners insist that temporary latrines must be built downhill and far away from community water sources?

options.A: To ensure the smell blows away from the tents
options.B: To prevent sewage from contaminating the community's drinking water supply
options.C: To keep the ground dry and prevent mud
options.D: To make them easier to clean with heavy machinery

explanation: Gravity makes liquid flow downhill. If toilets are uphill from wells or streams, waste will wash straight into the drinking water. Basic hygiene logic! [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h4)

question: What patient detail is usually written on an ADR form to protect their privacy?

options.A: National ID number
options.B: Home address
options.C: Initials
options.D: Full residential phone number

explanation: Using just the patient's initials keeps their identity confidential while still letting the clinical team trace the record if needed. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the main reason we use patient isolation in the hospital?

options.A: To reduce the overall cost of hospital supplies
options.B: To punish patients who refuse to take their prescribed medication
options.C: To stop germs from spreading to other patients and staff
options.D: To give the patient a quiet room for undisturbed rest

explanation: You got this! Isolation acts as a shield to keep infectious bugs contained so that everyone else on the ward stays safe and healthy. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of secondary data in a community assessment?

options.A: Direct observation of stagnant water behind residential houses
options.B: A brand new questionnaire filled out by household heads today
options.C: Interviews conducted by the nurse with mothers in the market
options.D: Past clinic attendance registers and local census reports

explanation: Secondary data refers to information that has already been collected and recorded by someone else for other purposes. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: When giving ear drops to an adult patient, how should you pull the outer ear (pinna)?

options.A: Forward and down
options.B: Down and back
options.C: Straight outward
options.D: Up and back

explanation: A classic clinical tip! For adults, pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the wiggly ear canal so the drops flow smoothly all the way down. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h7)

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to share a patient's health record details?

options.A: With local journalists investigating clinic operations
options.B: With members of the direct healthcare team who are actively involved in caring for that patient
options.C: With family members who call the clinic demanding information over the phone
options.D: With curious community members asking about their neighbors

explanation: Patient privacy is sacred. Only share health details with the professionals directly helping to treat that specific patient. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h8)

question: Which organism usually causes eye infection symptoms to show up the earliest, often within 2 to 5 days after birth?

options.A: Herpes simplex virus
options.B: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: You're doing great! Gonococcal eye infections act fast, showing severe signs within just a few days of life. Quick action saves sight! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h3)

question: What is the main job of memory cells in our immune system?

options.A: To fight off future exposures to the same pathogen much faster
options.B: To signal the brain when body temperature rises
options.C: To digest dead red blood cells in the spleen
options.D: To produce extra red blood cells during heavy bleeding

explanation: Think of memory cells as the immune system's security cameras—they remember past germs so the body can crush them instantly next time! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T11#GNS313_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the main goal of Psychological First Aid (PFA) right after a disaster?

options.A: Forcing victims to recount every painful detail of the event
options.B: Providing humane practical support and reducing immediate distress
options.C: Conducting deep psychoanalysis to cure chronic personality disorders
options.D: Prescribing high-dose psychiatric medications to every survivor

explanation: You got this! PFA is all about offering a comforting presence, safety, and practical help—not forcing people into heavy therapy right away. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h7)

question: During antenatal care for a multiple pregnancy, what should be a key focus of your nursing care?

options.A: Monitoring for early signs of preterm labor
options.B: Encouraging complete bed rest for all nine months
options.C: Stopping all routine ultrasound evaluations
options.D: Recommending a low-calorie diet to limit weight gain

explanation: Correct! Teaching mums to spot early tightenings or pressure, and making sure they keep their clinic visits, are top priorities to catch preterm labor early. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T018#GNS226_U2_T018_h5)

question: What is your main nursing duty when giving drugs to stop excessive bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Encourage her to drink large amounts of oral rehydration fluids
options.B: Watch for the womb to contract and bleeding to slow down
options.C: Check her skin for rashes every five minutes
options.D: Keep the patient flat with her legs raised high

explanation: These drugs work by making the womb muscle squeeze tight, closing off those bleeding vessels. You're doing great with your medication checks! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h5)

question: What is the most important rule when picking a theoretical framework for your study?

options.A: It must be a grand theory rather than a middle-range theory
options.B: It must be approved by the hospital nursing director
options.C: It must naturally match the specific research problem and variables
options.D: It must be the most recently published theory in nursing literature

explanation: Right! Your framework has to make logical sense with what you are trying to find out. Never force a mismatch. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which human infectious disease is the only one successfully eradicated globally so far?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Malaria
options.C: Measles
options.D: Smallpox

explanation: Correct! Through a massive worldwide vaccination campaign led by the WHO, smallpox was completely wiped out. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using mobile outreach teams in immunization programs?

options.A: To sell prescription medications directly to rural households
options.B: To reach children living in remote or hard-to-access communities
options.C: To collect taxes from local markets on behalf of the government
options.D: To replace permanent primary health centers in major cities

explanation: You got it! Mobile teams bridge the gap so children in hard-to-reach areas don't miss out on life-saving vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of table footnotes in a research paper?

options.A: To list the names of all the study participants
options.B: To provide a detailed biography of the researcher
options.C: To hide data that does not support the hypothesis
options.D: To define abbreviations and symbols used in the table

explanation: Footnotes explain abbreviations like SD or CI so readers can easily interpret the table elements. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why does the egg trigger the cortical reaction right after a sperm gets inside?

options.A: To block entry by additional sperm cells
options.B: To double the size of the egg cell
options.C: To trigger the first mitotic division
options.D: To stimulate the release of progesterone

explanation: Spot on! The egg quickly puts up a chemical shield so no extra sperm can enter, ensuring the right amount of genetic material. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T3#GNS121_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why is relying purely on old habits and trial-and-error risky in nursing?

options.A: It is usually too expensive for the hospital to fund
options.B: It takes too much paperwork to document
options.C: It can compromise patient safety and clinical outcomes
options.D: It prevents nurses from working in private clinics

explanation: Exactly! Doing things just because 'we've always done it that way' can sometimes hurt patients. We always want our care backed by solid evidence. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why does early child marriage put young mothers at high risk for severe birth complications?

options.A: Adolescent girls have natural immunity that destroys fetal blood cells
options.B: Early pregnancy causes a sudden drop in maternal red blood cell production
options.C: Young brides are legally prohibited from visiting antenatal care clinics
options.D: The young mother's pelvis and reproductive organs may not be fully developed

explanation: A young girl's body is often still growing. If she gets pregnant too early, her pelvis may be too small, leading to obstructed labor and serious emergencies. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T5#GNS312_U4_T5_h5)

question: What actually happens when a patient experiences hormone resistance?

options.A: Target cell receptors fail to respond to normal hormone levels
options.B: The pituitary gland blocks the bloodstream to the target tissue
options.C: The liver destroys circulating hormones before they reach organs
options.D: The endocrine gland completely stops producing all chemical messengers

explanation: Imagine knocking on a door (the hormone), but the doorbell is broken so nobody answers (the cell receptor). The hormone is present in the blood, but the cells just won't listen to it! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h2)

question: Which organ is primarily responsible for filtering and excreting water-soluble drug waste?

options.A: Kidneys
options.B: Lungs
options.C: Spleen
options.D: Skin

explanation: Your kidneys are your body's ultimate filters. They continuously clean your blood and flush out water-soluble drug breakdown products through your urine. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which clinical situation makes the rectal route most beneficial?

options.A: A patient who prefers taking pills with warm fruit juice
options.B: Routine daily administration of standard chewable vitamins
options.C: Persistent vomiting and inability to swallow oral medications
options.D: A patient who is fully alert and requesting oral painkillers

explanation: Persistent vomiting makes oral administration impossible, making the rectal route a safe and effective backup. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h5)

question: What is the main goal when a community nurse acts as an advocate for their patients?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations in local clinics
options.B: Financing private hospitals through personal funds
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties against sick community members
options.D: Speaking up for vulnerable groups to improve health resources

explanation: You're doing great! Being an advocate means being a voice for people who might not have the power or platform to speak up for their own health needs. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h4)

question: What should you do if you are holding a sterile instrument package and suddenly feel unsure if it's truly sterile?

options.A: Use it only if the outer wrapper looks clean
options.B: Consider it contaminated and discard it
options.C: Wipe the instrument down with an antiseptic
options.D: Ask the surgeon to inspect the item before use

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! Patient safety always comes first, so never take chances with a questionable sterile item. [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is the main job of ATP when it binds to myosin during muscle contraction?

options.A: To allow the myosin head to detach from actin
options.B: To release acetylcholine into the synapse
options.C: To pull the Z-lines further apart
options.D: To instantly activate the sarcoplasmic reticulum

explanation: ATP is the energy currency that acts like a release button, letting the myosin head disconnect from actin so it can reset for the next pull. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the name of the system used in Nigerian health facilities for reporting priority diseases and public health events?

options.A: International Airline Passenger Registry
options.B: Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR)
options.C: National Bank Financial Ledger
options.D: Global Air Traffic Control Network

explanation: Spot on! The IDSR framework is the backbone for tracking and reporting infectious diseases across Nigerian clinics. You're doing fantastic! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h7)

question: Under Nigerian law, what is a specific rule public organizations must follow regarding employment?

options.A: They must provide free housing for all disabled citizens.
options.B: They must exempt disabled individuals from paying any taxes.
options.C: They must allocate at least 5% of their workforce positions to persons with disabilities.
options.D: They must fund private medical clinics in every rural community.

explanation: The law sets a helpful employment quota requiring public establishments to reserve a minimum of 5% of their jobs for qualified persons with disabilities. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h2)

question: What two main ingredients are combined in the scientific method?

options.A: Tradition and personal intuition
options.B: Gut feelings and unverified habits
options.C: Rational logic and empirical observation
options.D: Strict authority and superstition

explanation: Science brings together logical thinking and real, measurable sensory data to test ideas properly. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is smoking a cigarette near oxygen therapy a massive fire hazard?

options.A: Smokers are unable to handle oxygen equipment properly
options.B: Oxygen tanks release toxic gases when heated by smoke
options.C: Cigarettes automatically explode when they touch oxygen tubing
options.D: Oxygen feeds fires and makes flames spread with explosive speed

explanation: Medical oxygen makes fires burn super fast and extremely hot. Even a small spark near oxygen can turn into a dangerous blaze instantly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T8#GNS324_U6_T8_h2)

question: As a nurse, why shouldn't you focus *only* on physical symptoms when caring for a client's reproductive health?

options.A: Because physical symptoms are rarely accurate indicators of reproductive disease
options.B: Because reproductive health includes mental, social, and bodily autonomy aspects
options.C: Because hospital policies strictly prohibit treating only physical complaints
options.D: Because laboratory tests cannot detect most reproductive system infections

explanation: You are caring for a human being, not just a body! Since reproductive health covers mental and social wellness too, great nurses look at the big picture. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h1)

question: Blood from under the tongue flows directly into which major vein on its way to the heart?

options.A: Renal artery
options.B: Hepatic portal vein
options.C: Femoral vein
options.D: Internal jugular vein

explanation: You've got this! The sublingual veins drain straight into the internal jugular vein to reach the heart quickly. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h2)

question: Which of these heart rhythms will actually cause an AED to advise and deliver a shock?

options.A: Asystole
options.B: Atrial Fibrillation
options.C: Sinus Bradycardia
options.D: Ventricular Fibrillation

explanation: Ventricular Fibrillation (VFib) is a shockable rhythm where the heart's ventricles just quiver instead of pumping. The AED recognizes this and delivers the reset shock. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h3)

question: What nutritional guidance should a home health nurse give to a newly postpartum breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Stop drinking water with meals to prevent overhydration.
options.B: Increase daily calorie and fluid intake to support milk production.
options.C: Avoid all dairy products to improve the baby's digestion.
options.D: Immediately start a strict low-calorie diet to lose pregnancy weight.

explanation: Breastfeeding burns extra calories and requires higher fluid intake to maintain a healthy milk supply and keep the mother energized. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the normal, healthy look of a newly made intestinal stoma?

options.A: Pink to brick-red
options.B: Bright yellow or green
options.C: Dark purple to black
options.D: Pale white or gray

explanation: Correct! A healthy stoma is packed with tiny blood vessels, which gives it a nice moist, pink to brick-red color. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h3)

question: Which of these should normally NOT slip through the kidney's filter into your urine?

options.A: Sodium mineral ions
options.B: Filtered water molecules
options.C: Large plasma proteins
options.D: Dissolved glucose molecules

explanation: Correct! A healthy kidney filter has tiny pores that keep big things like proteins and blood cells safely inside your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h2)

question: What are the three small bones found inside the middle ear?

options.A: Tympanics
options.B: Cochlea
options.C: Turbinates
options.D: Ossicles

explanation: The malleus, incus, and stapes are collectively known as the ossicles, which transmit sound vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in the hospital?

options.A: Tracking hospital supply inventory and ordering new medical equipment
options.B: Managing staff work schedules and payroll calculations
options.C: Providing entertainment options for clients staying overnight
options.D: Serving as a digital version of a client's comprehensive medical chart

explanation: An EHR is simply your patient's complete medical history, lab results, and notes kept safely in one digital folder. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: What test is always needed to give a 100% definitive diagnosis of cancer?

options.A: Tissue biopsy
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Ultrasound scan

explanation: Scans and blood tests give us great clues, but looking at a tiny tissue sample under a microscope is what confirms cancer for sure. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h5)

question: In a risk pool, what happens to the money paid by members who stay completely healthy?

options.A: Their unused contributions help pay for the medical care of sick members
options.B: The insurance scheme is forced to shut down immediately
options.C: Their money is refunded in cash at the end of every month
options.D: They are penalized with higher premium rates next year

explanation: Great job! Risk pooling works because the contributions of healthy members cover the costs of those who fall ill, balancing everything out. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h5)

question: In reproductive health counseling, what does "dual protection" mean?

options.A: Taking two different types of oral contraceptive pills every morning
options.B: Using condoms alongside a hormonal or reversible contraceptive method
options.C: Involving both parents and guardians in the family planning decision
options.D: Visiting the clinic twice a month for routine medical checkups

explanation: You got it! Dual protection means doubling down on safety: using a barrier method (like condoms) to stop infections plus reliable birth control to prevent pregnancy. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h3)

question: A mother gave birth 20 minutes ago. What is the most critical nursing check right now in the recovery ward?

options.A: assessing maternal vital signs and checking the firmness of the uterus
options.B: encouraging immediate ambulation to prevent deep vein thrombosis
options.C: performing a digital internal examination to check for retained membranes
options.D: initiating strict fluid restriction to allow the bladder to rest

explanation: You nailed it! Checking vital signs and making sure the uterus feels firm helps us catch and prevent postpartum hemorrhage early. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h4)

question: What is the hallmark feature of primary (essential) hypertension?

options.A: It only occurs in individuals over the age of eighty
options.B: It has no single identifiable underlying medical cause
options.C: It resolves spontaneously without any lifestyle changes
options.D: It always develops suddenly due to kidney failure

explanation: Most high blood pressure is 'primary'—meaning it builds up slowly over time without one single clear-cut medical culprit like a diseased kidney. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is an early sign of developing shock that you should watch out for in trauma patients?

options.A: High urine output
options.B: Altered mental status and cool skin
options.C: Warm, flushed skin
options.D: Slow and deep breathing

explanation: You nailed it. When the body goes into shock, blood gets pulled away from the skin and brain, making the patient feel anxious or confused with cool, clammy hands. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h4)

question: When a patient needs both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, why should the bronchodilator be used first?

options.A: It stops the side effects of the steroid from harming the heart
options.B: It neutralizes stomach acid that might interfere with breathing
options.C: It opens the airways so the steroid can reach deeper into the lungs
options.D: It cleans the mouth so the patient does not develop a fungal infection

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first widens the bronchial tubes, allowing the corticosteroid to penetrate further down into the respiratory tree. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is a normal finding right after Gallows traction is removed?

options.A: Complete loss of feeling in both legs
options.B: One leg suddenly growing longer than the other
options.C: Running and walking right away without help
options.D: Stiffness in the hips and knees from lying still

explanation: Keeping those little legs up in the air for weeks makes the joints stiff. Gentle stretching and movement will get them back to normal in no time! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h7)

question: When we talk about 'food availability' in healthcare and nutrition, what does it mainly mean?

options.A: The physical presence of food in a specific area
options.B: The personal preference for certain foods
options.C: The ability of a person to cook a meal
options.D: The amount of money a government saves

explanation: Food availability simply means that food is physically there in the community—whether through local farming, imports, or stored supplies. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T021#GNS227_U2_T021_h1)

question: What is a major disadvantage of bilateral tubal ligation compared to barrier methods like condoms?

options.A: It requires daily motivation and adherence from the client.
options.B: It immediately causes early menopause and hot flashes.
options.C: It has a very high failure rate within the first year.
options.D: It offers no protection against sexually transmitted infections.

explanation: While highly effective at preventing pregnancy, tubal ligation does not shield against sexually transmitted infections, unlike barrier methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: In nursing research, what does 'validity' simply mean?

options.A: How truly a study measures what it claims to measure
options.B: How fast a computer can run the data
options.C: Whether the paper was published in a big journal
options.D: How many patients took part in the study

explanation: Think of validity as truthfulness! It just checks if the research tool or study is actually measuring what it says it is measuring. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is a key duty when taking a patient's medication history?

options.A: Prescribing new antibiotics if the patient feels weak
options.B: Asking specifically about self-prescribed drugs, herbs, and leftover pills
options.C: Telling the patient to stop asking questions about their treatment
options.D: Selling safe over-the-counter drugs directly from the nursing station

explanation: That's right! Always dig deeper during assessments to find out what informal remedies or leftover pills the patient has taken. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h8)

question: How do monitoring devices improve nursing documentation?

options.A: By transmitting captured data directly into electronic health records
options.B: By erasing old vital signs every twelve hours
options.C: By forcing nurses to write everything on paper charts first
options.D: By locking all patient data so other staff cannot read it

explanation: Connecting bedside devices to digital records cuts down on manual entry mistakes and saves time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h1)

question: In a healthy human body, where do normal prion proteins naturally live?

options.A: Along the lining of the gut
options.B: On the membranes of neurons
options.C: Inside red blood cells
options.D: Within the fluid of joints

explanation: You got it! Normal prions hang out peacefully on the surface membranes of our nerve cells. It's only when they change shape that trouble starts. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h2)

question: What laboratory check is needed to tell Taenia saginata and Taenia solium apart with certainty?

options.A: Performing a chest X-ray to check for lung consolidation
options.B: Checking serum electrolyte levels for chronic dehydration
options.C: Examining the uterine branches of intact passed proglottids
options.D: Measuring total white blood cell counts in a routine blood sample

explanation: You got it! Lab techs count the side branches in the uterus of an intact passed segment to easily tell the two species apart. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h5)

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance for infectious diseases?

options.A: Ongoing collection and analysis of health data to guide public health action
options.B: Enforcing strict legal penalties for healthcare facilities that break sterile technique
options.C: Manufacture of safe and effective vaccines for global distribution
options.D: Providing emergency medical treatment to individual hospital patients

explanation: Correct! Tracking disease numbers helps public health teams spot trends and stop outbreaks early. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h8)

question: Why can't a nurse just assume a community health program will run on autopilot once planned?

options.A: Written plans are legally required to change every single week
options.B: Daily operational challenges and local realities require constant active adaptation
options.C: Funding is automatically withdrawn as soon as the implementation phase begins
options.D: Community members lose interest before the first day of service delivery

explanation: Fieldwork is full of surprises! Things like sudden shortages mean you have to think on your feet rather than blindly following a rigid script. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h1)

question: Why can an untreated lower vaginal infection lead to problems with getting pregnant?

options.A: Infections can travel upward through the uterus and scar the fallopian tubes
options.B: Bacterial toxins permanently stop the pituitary gland from releasing hormones
options.C: Inflammation completely closes the outer vaginal opening with scar tissue
options.D: Microbes directly destroy all developing eggs stored inside the ovaries

explanation: Spot on! Infections can move up (like in pelvic inflammatory disease) and leave scars that block the tubes, making it hard for eggs to travel. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h7)

question: During a hospital food poisoning investigation, who makes the best control group?
