options.A: Healthy volunteers recruited from a local university far away from the hospital
options.B: Patients admitted to the same hospital who did not eat the contaminated food and have no gastrointestinal illness
options.C: Patients who have recovered from the same food poisoning outbreak
options.D: Doctors and nurses who worked in the hospital kitchen

explanation: Great choice! Good controls come from the same environment and background population, but are thankfully free of the illness. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h2)

question: What is the primary function of vitamins in the human body?

options.A: Building thick outer walls around every body cell
options.B: Storing excess fat inside the abdominal cavity
options.C: Supplying the majority of daily caloric energy
options.D: Acting as coenzymes to regulate metabolic pathways

explanation: Vitamins do not provide calories, but they work as coenzymes to help chemical reactions run smoothly in the body. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h3)

question: What is the best household method to prevent tumbu fly infestations from clothes in Nigeria?

options.A: Ironing all washed clothes with a hot iron
options.B: Sprinkling heavy perfumes on garments before wearing
options.C: Drying clothes indoors inside closed plastic bags
options.D: Soaking clothes in salty cold water overnight

explanation: The intense heat from a hot iron easily destroys any fly eggs left on damp clothes drying outside. Simple prevention saves lives! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which group of vitamins needs dietary fat to be properly absorbed by your gut?

options.A: All known synthetic vitamins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins like A, D, E, and K
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins like B and C
options.D: Only vitamin C and iron

explanation: Think of dietary fat as the vehicle that helps fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K) travel across your intestinal wall into your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h2)

question: Think of a theoretical framework as the backbone of a nursing study. What is its main job?

options.A: Providing funding for data collection and equipment
options.B: Serving as the structural foundation and guide for the study
options.C: Determining the exact sample size needed for the project
options.D: Writing the final reference list in the correct format

explanation: Spot on! Just like a physical building needs a strong frame to stand, a research study needs a theoretical framework to shape how it is designed and understood. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is the main goal of active case finding by a community health nurse?

options.A: Collecting accurate financial data for the local government health department
options.B: Reducing the number of patients who visit the clinic for minor headaches
options.C: Finding infected individuals early before they develop severe illness or spread the disease
options.D: Punishing families who refuse to bring their children for routine immunizations

explanation: Active case finding involves going into the community to identify sick people early, allowing prompt treatment and halting further transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h6)

question: What should a nurse do if a low-risk pregnant woman develops severe anemia during her third trimester?

options.A: Advise her to drink more local herbal tea
options.B: Allow her to deliver at home with extra pillows
options.C: Disqualify her from home delivery and refer her to a hospital
options.D: Ignore the blood test results if she feels fine

explanation: Severe anemia puts the mother at high risk of postpartum hemorrhage, meaning she must deliver where blood transfusion is available. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a factor that helps sustain an endemic disease in a community?

options.A: Low childhood immunization rates
options.B: Universal access to clean water
options.C: Inadequate waste management
options.D: Poor housing construction

explanation: Clean water actually stops diseases from spreading! Poor sanitation and lack of clean water are what help infections stick around. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h5)

question: What does drug non-compliance mean in nursing practice?

options.A: A doctor writing an illegible prescription slip
options.B: A nurse administering the wrong dose of medication
options.C: A pharmacy running out of essential prescribed drugs
options.D: A patient failing to follow a prescribed medication regimen

explanation: Non-compliance simply means the patient is not taking their drugs the way the doctor or nurse instructed them to. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: How is Ultra-High Temperature (UHT) milk different from standard pasteurized milk?

options.A: UHT milk contains chemical preservatives instead of heat treatment
options.B: UHT milk can remain shelf-stable at room temperature until opened
options.C: UHT milk is boiled slowly on a stove for several hours
options.D: UHT milk requires continuous refrigeration from farm to table

explanation: Brilliant! UHT uses super high heat that wipes out practically all microbes, meaning you can store it on your shelf without a fridge until you pop it open. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h5)

question: If you are talking to local village elders about building a new maternity clinic, how should you pitch it?

options.A: Discuss advanced surgical techniques used in teaching hospitals
options.B: Focus on family health, community safety, and local traditions
options.C: Present complex statistical models on maternal mortality ratios
options.D: Emphasize strict government legal codes and budget allocations

explanation: You're doing great! Village elders want to hear about real, practical things that protect and respect their families and community traditions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h2)

question: What is a major objective of public health surveillance programs?

options.A: Detecting epidemics early to stop transmission
options.B: Reducing the cost of medical equipment
options.C: Increasing the number of hospital beds
options.D: Providing free medications to the public

explanation: Early detection allows health workers to step in quickly and block the spread of infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which group of medical parasites is made up of tiny, single-celled organisms?

options.A: Nematodes
options.B: Cestodes
options.C: Protozoa
options.D: Helminths

explanation: Think 'proto' as in primitive or single. Protozoa are microscopic, single-celled fighters that can multiply super fast inside you. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h3)

question: A client vomits twenty minutes after taking her emergency contraceptive pill. What should you do?

options.A: Ignore the vomiting because it has no effect on the medication
options.B: Consult the provider to see if a repeat dose is needed
options.C: Give her a high dose of intravenous antibiotics immediately
options.D: Tell her the pill failed and she must schedule surgery

explanation: If she vomits shortly after taking the pill (within two hours), her body might not have absorbed the medicine. Always check with the clinician if she needs another dose! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: Which hormone acts on the collecting duct to increase water reabsorption during dehydration?

options.A: Erythropoietin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH)
options.D: Thyroid hormone

explanation: ADH triggers water channels to open in the collecting ducts, letting water return to the bloodstream instead of passing out as urine. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is a major emotional and social challenge that HIV-positive mums often face regarding how they feed their babies?

options.A: Complete lack of interest in infant nutritional needs
options.B: Legal restrictions against breastfeeding in public places
options.C: Inability to find pediatric clinics in rural areas
options.D: Fear of stigma and disclosure within their communities

explanation: The fear of being judged or accidentally revealing their status to family and neighbors weighs heavily on many mums. Empathy goes a long way! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T12#GNS216_U6_T12_h6)

question: Why do we need our research questions to be very clear and specific?

options.A: To confuse readers who are not nurses
options.B: To ensure the study collects relevant and measurable data
options.C: To prevent the ethics committee from reading the proposal
options.D: To make the proposal document as long as possible

explanation: Clear questions keep you on track so you don't end up collecting information you don't need! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h4)

question: Generally speaking, what is the trade-off between joint mobility and stability?

options.A: There is no connection between mobility and stability
options.B: Greater stability usually means greater speed of movement
options.C: Mobility and stability always increase together
options.D: Greater mobility usually means lower stability

question: What is the correct way to wipe when cleaning a female patient's private parts (perineal care)?

options.A: From the pubic area toward the anus
options.B: From the anus toward the tummy
options.C: Wiping sideways across the area
options.D: In tiny circles all over

explanation: Correct! Always wipe front-to-back. This keeps germs from the back passage away from the urinary opening, stopping nasty infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is a common consequence of poor communication during the implementation phase?

options.A: Immediate dismissal of the local village traditional ruler
options.B: Low community turnout and poor participation in health activities
options.C: A sudden surplus of expired medical vaccines
options.D: Instant failure of government financial auditing systems

explanation: If people do not know when or where a health outreach is happening, they cannot attend, resulting in low turnout. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: What bedside tool do nurses use to check the depth of a patient's muscle relaxation?

options.A: Bedside blood glucose meter
options.B: Peripheral nerve stimulator
options.C: Manual blood pressure cuff
options.D: Incentive spirometry device

explanation: A peripheral nerve stimulator gives tiny, safe zaps to check nerve and muscle response (the train-of-four test). Great tool for safe nursing care! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h6)

question: What must a nurse researcher obtain before starting any experiment involving human subjects?

options.A: A grant from a pharmaceutical company
options.B: Ethical approval from a review board
options.C: Approval from local newspaper reporters
options.D: Permission to buy new uniforms

explanation: Patient safety and rights must be protected, so an ethics committee must review and approve the study plan first. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h6)

question: How do membrane drug transporters affect how medications move in the body?

options.A: By filtering large molecules directly out of the bloodstream
options.B: By neutralizing toxic metabolites before they reach the liver
options.C: By controlling how drugs move across cell barriers and into tissues
options.D: By creating permanent chemical bonds with circulating plasma proteins

explanation: You got it! Think of transporters as cellular gatekeepers that decide when and how drugs cross into our tissues and cells. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane called?

options.A: Active transport
options.B: Pinocytosis
options.C: Simple diffusion
options.D: Osmosis

explanation: Osmosis is the specific term for the passive movement of water molecules across a membrane from an area of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why are lower respiratory infections generally more serious than upper respiratory ones?

options.A: They cause severe localized pain in the nose.
options.B: They only happen to people with heart disease.
options.C: They directly interfere with oxygen exchange in the air sacs.
options.D: They are always completely resistant to drugs.

explanation: You've got this! When an infection hits the tiny air sacs (alveoli) deep in the lungs, it blocks oxygen from getting into the blood, making it much harder to breathe. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the main activity during the 'Plan' phase of the PDSA cycle?

options.A: Punishing staff who fail to follow new guidelines
options.B: Setting a clear objective and planning how to test a change
options.C: Purchasing expensive medical equipment for the ward
options.D: Permanently rewriting all hospital policy rulebooks

explanation: Well done! In the Plan phase, we figure out our goal and decide exactly how we want to run our little test. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h3)

question: How do cholinesterase inhibitor drugs work in the brain?

options.A: By destroying excess beta-amyloid protein deposits
options.B: By preventing the breakdown of acetylcholine
options.C: By blocking all electrical impulses in nerve cells
options.D: By increasing the physical size of brain tissue

explanation: Exactly right! They stop the enzyme that destroys acetylcholine, keeping more of this vital memory chemical active in the brain. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T2#GNS222_U4_T2_h4)

question: What happens when data collection for a quality project takes too much nursing time?

options.A: The government awards the hospital a special safety prize
options.B: Patients begin recording their own vital signs daily
options.C: Staff may fabricate numbers just to fill out the forms
options.D: Hospital printers automatically run out of official paper

explanation: Overly burdensome data entry leads to burnout and inaccurate reporting because bedside time is precious. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h4)

question: How do adults usually approach learning differently from children?

options.A: Adults memorize facts faster without needing to understand the reason

options.C: Drugs that cause severe tissue damage if they leak outside the vein
options.D: Medications that are only given orally in pill form

explanation: Vesicants are tricky drugs! If they escape the vein into the skin, they can cause blistering and tissue damage, which is why nurses watch IV sites so closely. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h3)

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because they saw dead worms in the toilet after starting their deworming pills. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop taking the medication immediately
options.B: Advise the patient to take a double dose to kill remaining live worms
options.C: Reassure the patient that this is a normal expected result of the treatment
options.D: Tell the patient to report to the emergency room for a blood transfusion

explanation: Fantastic! Reassure them—seeing dead worms in the stool just means the medication is doing its exact job and clearing them out! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h8)

question: What is the biggest hurdle when trying to treat brain tumors using regular systemic chemotherapy drugs?

options.A: Chemotherapy drugs only work on bones and muscles.
options.B: Chemotherapy causes permanent blindness in every patient.
options.C: Brain tissue absorbs too much medication and dissolves instantly.
options.D: The blood-brain barrier blocks many drugs from entering the brain tissue.

explanation: You got it! The blood-brain barrier is like a strict security guard—it protects the brain from toxins, but unfortunately, it also blocks many helpful chemotherapy drugs from getting inside. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which variable always goes on the bottom (horizontal X-axis) of a scatter diagram?

options.A: The average median score
options.B: The dependent outcome
options.C: The independent variable
options.D: The total patient count

explanation: Remember: the independent (or explanatory) variable always sits comfortably on the horizontal X-axis. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h3)

question: Why are accurate health records so important in busy primary health care clinics?

options.A: They ensure continuity of care when different health workers see the same patient over time.
options.B: They are used to calculate monthly staff salaries.
options.C: They replace physical exams when the clinic is crowded.
options.D: They guarantee the clinic gets international donor funds.

explanation: Patients often see different nurses on different days. Good records ensure the next nurse knows exactly what treatment was given, keeping the patient safe and cared for smoothly! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which everyday substance must definitely be kept out of a stool sample?

options.A: Normal saline
options.B: Tap water
options.C: Paper towels
options.D: Urine

explanation: Urine mixes easily with stool and can ruin lab tests for parasites or blood. Always ask patients to pass urine first! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical community resource recommended for families with an infant?

options.A: Lactation consultant services
options.B: Early childhood intervention programs
options.C: Adult vocational retraining centers
options.D: Immunization and vaccination clinics

explanation: Correct! Vocational centers are for adult job training. Families with infants need resources focused on child health, feeding, and early development. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the primary action of a bacteriostatic antibiotic?

options.A: Instantly dissolving the cell wall of all viruses
options.B: Stopping the reproduction and growth of bacteria
options.C: Lowering the patient's fever by acting on the brain
options.D: Stimulating the patient's bone marrow to make platelets

explanation: Bacteriostatic drugs hit the pause button on bacterial multiplication so the body's natural immune system can easily finish clearing them out. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of these actions is a big NO-MAKE for infection control at the bedside?

options.A: Performing hand hygiene before entering the room
options.B: Reusing disposable gloves between different patients
options.C: Cleaning stethoscope tubing between patient checks
options.D: Using appropriate personal protective equipment

explanation: Spot on! Disposable gloves are strictly single-use. Reusing them spreads germs from patient to patient—always grab a fresh pair! [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h7)

question: Who represents the primary user group of Electronic Health Record systems in a hospital setting?

options.A: Nurses
options.B: Facility maintenance staff
options.C: Hospital accountants
options.D: External software developers

explanation: Nurses document the largest share of daily patient care data, making them the primary users of clinical EHR systems. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: How should a nurse handle conflicting cultural or religious burial requests?

options.A: Accommodate the beliefs respectfully while following hospital policy
options.B: Refuse to participate in the care of the deceased patient
options.C: Ignore the family requests and follow standard hospital routine
options.D: Insist that the hospital rules override all personal beliefs

explanation: Nurses must balance standard safety protocols with deep respect for the cultural and religious traditions of the deceased and their family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)
